item.title: ADJUSTMENT IN HUDSON YARDS DISTRICT IMPROVEMENT BONUS CONTRIBUTION AMOUNT
item.description:
City Planning | Special Materials | Notice

ADJUSTMENT IN HUDSON YARDS DISTRICT IMPROVEMENT BONUS CONTRIBUTION AMOUNT

 

As provided in Section 93-31 of the Zoning Resolution of the City of New York, the required contribution amount per square foot of bonused floor area available through the District Improvement Fund Bonus in the Special Hudson Yards District has been increased from $169.68 per square foot to $175.62 per square foot as of August 1, 2026. 

In accordance with Section 93-31, this increase is based on the change in the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (CPI), as published by the U.S. Department of Labor, Bureau of Labor Statistics.  The CPI change for the period between July 1, 2025 and July 1, 2026 was an increase of 3.5 percent.

This increased contribution amount per square foot of bonused floor area applies to all contributions pursuant to Section 93-31 received after July 31, 2026, until s…

item.title: Alternative to Placement and Aftercare Services Concept Report
item.description:
Administration for Children's Services | Special Materials | Notice

Through the upcoming RFP, the Division of Youth and Family Justice (DYFJ) will continue its Juvenile Justice Initiative's (JJI) commitment to providing high-quality, evidenced-based interventions for youth at the highest level of need in the juvenile delinquency system - those being recommended for out-of-home placement and those exiting placement and reentering the community.  The upcoming RFP seeks highly experienced service providers to provide both alternative-to-placement (ATP) and placement aftercare services to youth ages 12 to 18 (up to age 17.5 at time of referral) and their families using targeted and specific evidenced-based interventions.  JJI serves youth who have been or are in the process of adjudication in New York City (NYC) juvenile courts. Intensive services allow them to remain at home while receiving support in the community, instead of being remanded to a juvenile justice setting. JJI services can be put in place for youth when leaving a juvenile justice non-secure or limited secure placement and transitioning back to the community. item.title: Prompt Payment Interest Rate July 1, 2026 - December 31, 2026
item.description:
Mayor's Office of Contract Services | Special Materials | Notice

Section 4-06 of the Procurement Policy Rules requires City agencies to process contract payments efficiently and expeditiously so as to assure timely contract payments to those suppliers doing business with the City. 

The Rule further requires that when payments are made after the Required Payment Date ('RPD'), interest, unless otherwise specified in the Rules, must be paid to the supplier. 

The Comptroller and the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) have jointly set the new Prompt Payment Interest Rate. The new Prompt Payment Interest Rate is 4.75% effective on payments for the six month period July 1, 2026 - December 31, 2026. 

 

Questions on this notice should be directed to: 

Kimberly Egbert  

Mayor's Office of Contract Services 

255 Greenwich Street, 9th Floor 

New York, NY 10007 

212-298-0887

kimberly.egbert@mocs.nyc.gov

item.title: Notice of Adopted Final Report
item.description:
Charter Revision Commission | Special Materials | Notice

NOTICE IS HEREBY GIVEN that the New York City Charter Revision Commission appointed in December 2025 has issued its Adopted Final Report, dated June 25, 2026. The Adopted Final Report is available for public review at: https://dechert.box.com/s/sk211wqnr9em96mi7mwpwwnjmy4ddsyu.

NOTICE IS FURTHER GIVEN that the Commissions ballot proposal to establish non-partisan local elections with open primaries was unanimously approved by the Commission for placement on the November 2026 General Election ballot. The ballot proposal was transmitted to the New York City Clerk on May 27, 2026, and, following the Commissions adoption of a revised and corrected amendment, was retransmitted on June 25, 2026. The ballot proposal and amended submission are available for public review at: https://dechert.box.com/s/qwga6ahtb8yzj3mpkh2mqkt6jo657ii9.
